..summary: README architecture tree omits src/research/ and lists CLI commands that no longer exist.

evidence: README.md:681-683 lists `commands/` as "monitor, doctor, config_check, history, watch"; only history.py, monitor.py and watch.py exist under src/cli/commands/.
The tree has no entry for src/research/ even though src/output/processor.py imports src.research.web_search and app.py's discover-web imports src.research.site_discovery.

The tree also omits src/output/domains/ and src/searcher/{pricing,query_language,listing_filter,sessions,selectors}.py, so it no longer predicts where code lives.

..summary: Notification channel send paths are untested outside console/webhook construction

evidence: tests/test_notification_channels.py only constructs ConsoleChannel and WebhookChannel and inspects attributes; `send()` is never awaited for any channel.

Coverage: src/notifications/channels/discord.py 23%, email.py 24%, system.py 24%, webhook.py 42%; payload construction and the False-on-failure branches of DiscordChannel.send and WebhookChannel.send are unexecuted.

EmailChannel's missing-configuration early return (email.py:24-28) and SystemChannel's per-platform subprocess branch (system.py:27-57) have no test, so the channel-selection and fallback contract is unpinned.
detail.suggestion: Add async tests that monkeypatch `aiohttp.ClientSession.post` (discord/webhook), `smtplib.SMTP` (email) and `subprocess.run` (system), then assert the outgoing payload and the False-on-non-2xx/exception contract, plus the unconfigured-email early return.

..summary: Launched browser contexts disable TLS verification and origin isolation for every site

evidence: src/browser/manager.py:95 sets ignore_https_errors=True for the persistent context and line 131 repeats it for the regular context.
src/browser/manager.py:101-102 adds --disable-web-security and --disable-features=IsolateOrigins,site-per-process to every persistent-context launch, with no per-site or config opt-in.
The default use_persistent_context: true path reuses ./browser_profile, so the profile that holds logged-in cookies runs without TLS or same-origin protection.
detail.suggestion: Add explicit BrowserConfig flags such as ignore_https_errors and disable_web_security (both default false), pass them only for profiles or sites that demonstrably need them, and keep anti-detection arguments separate from security-disabling arguments.

..summary: openpyxl is imported for Excel export but is not declared in any dependency manifest

..summary: src/searcher is both the domain model package and the application layer, creating five reciprocal package dependencies.

evidence: Package matrix shows reciprocal edges: agents<->searcher (agents/research/site_selection.py:11-12 imports SITES/SiteSpec/SiteCandidate; playwright_searcher.py:38 imports agents), config<->searcher (config/__init__.py:88 imports searcher.currency; searcher/filters.py:16 imports config.models), diagnostics<->searcher (diagnostics/selector_health.py:14 imports adapters.base; playwright_searcher.py:14 imports SelectorHealthTracker), llm<->searcher (llm/client.py:14 imports Deal; playwright_searcher.py:15 imports LLMClient), storage<->searcher (storage/manager.py:9-10 imports Deal/comparable_price; playwright_searcher.py:33 imports StorageManager).

src/searcher/playwright_searcher.py is an application orchestrator (821 LOC) that composes browser, LLM, storage, diagnostics and the optional agent pipeline; the same package also contains pure domain modules such as filters.py, pricing.py, site_profiles.py and site_registry.py.
src/searcher/adapters/base.py is imported by 34 modules, including src/storage/manager.py, src/output/processor.py, src/llm/client.py and src/intelligence/price_tracker.py.
detail.suggestion: Split src/searcher into a dependency-free domain package (models, filters, pricing, profiles, registry) and an application/search-runner package that composes browser, LLM, storage, diagnostics and agents. Extract the shared types first, then add an import-direction test that forbids infrastructure packages from importing the application layer.

..summary: storage.models defines a second, incompatible Deal/PriceHistory/WatchlistItem layer that looks canonical but is bypassed by the pipeline.

StorageManager itself imports Deal from src.searcher.adapters.base at src/storage/manager.py:9, not from src/storage/models.py, so the storage-layer model module is a shadow of the real one.
detail.suggestion: Create one canonical Deal module outside the scraper package (for example src/models/deal.py), migrate adapters, storage, output, LLM and watch to it, then delete src/storage/models.py and the getattr tolerance in record_price_sighting. Delete the unused storage PriceHistory/WatchlistItem duplicates; the live equivalents already exist next to their owners.

..summary: LLMClient mixes provider transport with deal-ranking policy and imports from both the agent and searcher packages.

evidence: src/llm/client.py:14 imports Deal from src.searcher.adapters.base; src/llm/client.py:284 imports validate_price_classification from src.searcher.pricing; the class implements refine_query, judge_results and rank_results over Deal at lines 557-654.

The open private-method issue only covers one helper; even after promoting that method, these domain methods and imports keep the layer inversion in place.
detail.suggestion: Keep LLMClient as a provider/transport class (chat, chat_json, fallback, health). Move deal query refinement, judging and ranking into a searcher-domain service, and move extract_json into a neutral src/llm/json_utils.py or src/text/json.py so both layers use the same helper.

..summary: load_config() mutates a process-wide rate table in searcher.currency, reversing the config-to-domain dependency direction.

evidence: src/config/__init__.py:86-90 imports set_rates from src.searcher.currency and calls it on every load_config() invocation.
src/config/models.py has 22 importer edges (including tests), so the lowest-level settings package carries an upward dependency into the domain.
src/searcher/currency.py:30 defines the mutable module-level _RATES; set_rates at :33-39 rebinds it with a global statement; to_eur at :135 silently falls back to that table.
src/searcher/adapters/base.py:189 calls parse_price_detail(text, self.currency) without a rates argument, so adapter prices depend on whichever config was loaded last in the process.
detail.suggestion: Remove set_rates from load_config and make the rate table an explicit input to the currency functions, or create a CurrencyRates object at the CLI composition root and pass it to adapters. If a process-wide table is kept, set it once in the application entry point and document it as bootstrap state rather than config-load side effect.

..summary: Site capabilities, trust metadata and status are duplicated across registry, config, profiles and adapter classes, and runtime reads different copies for different decisions.

evidence: src/searcher/site_registry.py:4-7 calls the registry the single source of truth for category coverage, but PlaywrightSearcher._site_matches at src/searcher/playwright_searcher.py:136-143 filters on WebsiteConfig.categories/conditions from config, and _filter_sites at :230-255 uses adapter class capabilities for registered sites.

src/searcher/site_registry.py:43-48 and src/searcher/adapters/alza.py:24-28 both define seller_type, has_warranty and warranty_note; src/output/processor.py:1329-1335 trusts the registry copy while selection trusts the adapter copy.

Registry status and profile status disagree for alza_cz: src/searcher/site_registry.py:150-155 says planned, src/searcher/site_profiles/alza_cz.yaml says blocked; _skip_reason at src/searcher/playwright_searcher.py:149-164 only consults profile readiness for planned sites without a registered adapter, so the profile's blocked status is ignored when the alza adapter exists.

Capability matching is implemented in at least three places: site_registry.sites_for, SiteCandidate.carries in src/searcher/site_selection.py:46-50 and SiteSelectionAgent._select_sites in src/agents/research/site_selection.py:72-80.
detail.suggestion: Give site metadata one owner. Either make SiteSpec authoritative and derive WebsiteConfig defaults and adapter capabilities from it, or reduce SiteSpec to identity and move capability/trust data into config/profiles. Add a single resolve_site_status(site_id, profile, adapter) used by selection, skip reasons and the sites command, and delete the duplicate adapter class attributes.

..summary: An unused page-object stack and a parallel selector table remain alongside the adapter/profile path, blurring which site-automation layer owns a site.

evidence: src/browser/pom/registry.py:21-27 maps alza, bazos, backmarket, ebay and facebook to page classes, but src/browser/pom/pages/__init__.py:5-23 aliases every site-specific class to the same generic SiteHome/SiteSearchResults/SiteProductDetail; no production module imports src.browser.pom, only tests/test_browser.py:2,7 and the POM package itself.
src/searcher/playwright_searcher.py:17-33 uses adapters and profiles and never constructs a POM page; README.md:683-684 still advertises browser/pom as the page-object layer.

src/searcher/selectors.py:7-127 is a second 11-site selector table; only scripts/discover_sites.py:33,210,619 uses it as a discovery bootstrap, while runtime extraction uses src/searcher/site_profiles/*.yaml.
detail.suggestion: Delete src/browser/pom and its test, or wire it and document it as the only page-object layer. Move the discovery bootstrap selectors into scripts/discover_sites.py (or read them from existing profiles) and remove src/searcher/selectors.py so discovery and runtime share one selector source.

..summary: Seven of eight agent classes do not subclass AgentBase; six plain classes plus one mixin-only class expose run() instead of execute(), leaving the advertised contract unused.

evidence: src/agents/base.py declares AgentBase as the "Base class for all agents in the Diamond Search pipeline", with abstract execute() and a concrete run() that supplies status tracking and error handling.

Only CoordinatorAgent subclasses AgentBase; DomainExpertAgent, MarketIntelAgent, LatestTechTrackerAgent, PriceHunterAgent, SiteSelectionAgent and RecommendationAgent are plain classes implementing async def run(input_data: dict) directly, and QueryExpansionAgent only inherits the LLMBackedAgent mixin.
CoordinatorAgent.__init__ annotates agents: list[AgentBase] (src/agents/coordinator.py:28), but its callers pass those non-subclasses, so the annotation does not describe reality.
Role typing drifts too: DomainExpertAgent uses AgentRole.DOMAIN_EXPERT while the other agents assign bare strings such as role = "price_hunter".
detail.suggestion: Choose one agent protocol and apply it to all eight: either make run(input)->dict the documented contract and drop execute/AgentBase from the type annotation, or migrate every agent to subclass AgentBase and implement execute(). Normalize role to AgentRole in the same pass.

..summary: Bazos and Facebook adapters never call detect_block, so anti-bot pages surface as empty results instead of SiteBlockedError.

evidence: AlzaAdapter.search, BackMarketAdapter.search, AmazonAdapter.search, eBayAdapter._collect_cards and ProfileAdapter.search all call await self.detect_block(page) and raise SiteBlockedError when it returns a reason.

BazosAdapter.search (src/searcher/adapters/bazos.py:39) and FacebookAdapter.search (src/searcher/adapters/facebook.py:28) call _goto_search and then wait for selectors without any detect_block call; neither module imports SiteBlockedError.
tests/test_adapters.py exercises block detection through get_adapter("bazos"), confirming the capability is expected for that adapter.
detail.suggestion: Call await self.detect_block(page) immediately after _goto_search in both adapters and raise SiteBlockedError with the returned reason; add a regression test that a challenge page raises rather than returning an empty list.

..summary: BackMarket and Facebook skip the shared price-quote pipeline, so their listings rank on the sticker price only.

evidence: Five concrete adapters (Alza, Amazon, Bazos, eBay, Profile) call extract_price_signals and attach build_price_quote(...) to Deal.price_quote.
BackMarketAdapter.extract_deal and FacebookAdapter.extract_deal construct Deal without price_quote; neither module imports src.searcher.pricing.
Deal.comparable_price_eur and the searcher ranking use the quote when present (pricing.py describes one comparable number), so shipping, promo and coupon text on these two sites is ignored.
detail.suggestion: Attach build_price_quote(price_eur, ...) from extract_price_signals(full_text, ...) in both adapters, even when the only signal is REGULAR, so every adapter returns the same populated Deal shape; add tests mirroring the existing Bazos/eBay quote tests.

..summary: CLI commands live in both src/cli/app.py and src/cli/commands/, with duplicate wrappers for run, doctor and config_check.

evidence: app.py contains 17 @app.command declarations and 27 top-level functions, including run, doctor, config_check, monitor and watch; only history_app, monitor and watch are imported from commands/.
commands/run.py defines run() that imports and calls app.run_async, and commands/doctor.py wraps app.doctor_async, while app.py separately defines its own run and doctor commands with the same names.

commands/config_check.py and commands/doctor.py have no production importer (test_cli.py only imports monitor and run), so identical command names can point at different implementations depending on the import path.
detail.suggestion: Adopt one ownership rule: move each command body into src/cli/commands/<name>.py and keep app.py for registration, or delete the unused wrappers and keep app.py as the only home. Update tests to the chosen entry point.

..summary: src/storage/models.py keeps a second Deal/WatchlistItem/PriceHistory model set that diverges from the canonical types.

evidence: src/storage/models.py defines Deal, PriceHistory and WatchlistItem; the rest of the code uses src/searcher/adapters/base.Deal, storage.manager.StoredDeal/PriceHistoryEntry and history.watchlist.WatchlistItem.
src/cli/commands/watch.py:118 imports src.storage.models.Deal inside a helper and passes it to StorageManager.record_price_sighting, whose parameter is annotated as the adapter Deal.
PriceHistory and WatchlistItem from storage.models are imported only by tests/test_storage.py, so the module survives without serving production code.
detail.suggestion: Delete the unused model definitions and import the canonical Deal in watch.py; if storage needs its own row models, keep them private to storage.manager and name them StoredDeal/PriceHistoryEntry so the two layers cannot be confused.

..summary: Coordinator flattens failed and budget-skipped agents to strings, so downstream .get() raises AttributeError

evidence: coordinator.py:14-22 _extract_result returns str(result.error) for a failed AgentResult and str(result) for an exception, erasing the failure type and traceback.
coordinator.py:135 stores bare strings for domain_expert and latest_tech, and 158 stores one for price_hunter, when a budget check fails; research and synthesis use an {"error": ...} dict instead.

coordinator.py:86 calls .get() on expertise_results['domain_expert'] and recommendation.py:55-56 does the same for domain_expert/latest_tech; a manual run with llm_call_budget=0 raised AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get', which AgentBase.run surfaced instead of 'Budget exceeded'.

The coordinator isolates research/expertise failures with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) (121,145) but awaits the price and synthesis agents directly (160,177), so an exception in those layers aborts the whole pipeline rather than becoming a per-agent failure.
detail.suggestion: Return {} or a small typed outcome (for example AgentOutcome(payload, error)) for every failure and budget skip, keep the reason in a separate errors map, and guard nested lookups. Route all four layers through one helper and add a budget=0 test asserting a clean failure result instead of AttributeError.

..summary: Watchlist save logs a disk error but callers report success, so failed writes are silently lost

evidence: history/watchlist.py:69-102 _save catches Exception, logs 'Failed to save watchlist' and returns None.
add_item calls _save at lines 129 and 143 and always returns the item; remove_item calls _save at 152 and returns True at 153 regardless of the write outcome.
The CLI prints 'Added to watchlist' at history.py:134 and 'Removed from watchlist' at 143 without inspecting any result, so a failed write is reported as success.
_load (53-67) logs and continues when the JSON is corrupt, leaving an empty in-memory list that the next add/remove overwrites over the original file.
detail.suggestion: Make _save return bool or raise a small WatchlistStorageError; propagate that to add_item/remove_item and have the CLI print Error: could not save watchlist: ... and exit 1. On load failure, back up or refuse to overwrite the corrupt file and add failure-path tests.

..summary: A crashed per-site search never reaches site_plan.skipped, so the report calls the site searched with zero deals

evidence: playwright_searcher.py:740-745 catches Exception, logs with logger.exception, records a failed health result and returns [] without appending to _skipped_sites.
Only the SiteBlockedError branch (726-739) appends a name/reason pair; site_plan (364-372) builds skipped solely from _skipped_sites.
processor.py:1859-1881 prints every name in site_plan.selected under 'Shops searched' and only site_plan.skipped under 'Skipped', so a crashed site is presented as searched with no deals.
detail.suggestion: Append {"name": site.name, "reason": f"search failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"} to _skipped_sites before returning [] (or add a separate failed list to SitePlan) and add a test whose adapter raises RuntimeError and then asserts the reason appears in site_plan.

..summary: CLI prompt/watchlist file reads bypass the Error/exit contract and produce raw tracebacks

evidence: app.py:445-449 opens --prompt-file and calls data.get('prompt', '') without guarding OSError or yaml.YAMLError, and without checking that safe_load returned a mapping.

watch.py:202-207 opens --watchlist with no guard; monitor.py:24-30 loads the YAML prompt file unguarded, and its top-level handler prints Error then re-raises at 173-177, so the traceback is still shown.
The established contract in the same CLI is typer.echo('Error: ...', err=True) followed by raise typer.Exit(1) from None (app.py:337-339 and 436-442).
detail.suggestion: Wrap each read in try/except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError), validate that the parsed value is a mapping, print Error: cannot read <path>: <exc> to stderr and raise typer.Exit(1) from None. Add CliRunner tests for a missing file and a YAML scalar.

..summary: Registry lookups use three miss conventions and output.domain is never validated, so a typo crashes reporting

evidence: output.domains.registry.get raises KeyError (registry.py:27-29), searcher.adapters.get_adapter raises ValueError (adapters/__init__.py:22-27), and site_registry.by_id returns None (site_registry.py:330-335).
processor.py:120 reads OutputConfig.domain into domain_override without validation and detect() forwards it to get() at registry.py:39; config/models.py:96 types it as a bare str.

Manual check: AppConfig().output.domain='typo_domain' followed by _heuristic_analysis(Deal(...)) raised KeyError: 'typo_domain' after the search had already run, so report generation crashes at the last step.
detail.suggestion: Validate output.domain once (pydantic validator on OutputConfig or processor init) and either warn plus fall back to GENERIC or emit the same Error: unknown domain ... exit. Standardize registry misses on one contract, preferably a shared LookupError subclass or None with explicit caller handling, and add a test for an unknown config domain.

..summary: British spellings remain in identifiers and docstrings while the codebase uses American forms.

evidence: src/searcher/filters.py uses normalised and normalised_key at lines 218-220, 403-407 and 431-502 while the same module defines _normalize_choice and _normalize_condition.
src/output/domains/base.py:79-87 uses normalised, but src/output/processor.py:829 defines a nested helper named normalized, so both spellings appear in the same pipeline.

detail.suggestion: Standardize on the American forms already used by normalize.py and normalize_specs: rename normalised to normalized, normalised_key to normalized_key, localise_query to localize_query, _centimetres to _centimeters, NEIGHBOURS to NEIGHBORS, and update the three docstrings and section comment.

..summary: The same site key is called name, id, site_id and site_name, and site_name can hold a hostname.

evidence: WebsiteConfig.name (src/config/models.py:29) is the registry key such as 'alza', while SiteSpec.name (src/searcher/site_registry.py:24) is the display label and SiteSpec.id is the key.

Deal.site_name (src/searcher/adapters/base.py:44) is populated from profile.site_id (src/searcher/adapters/profile_adapter.py:175) and site.name (src/searcher/playwright_searcher.py:723), so it is the key rather than a human-readable name.

SiteCandidate.id and SiteCandidate.name are both set to site.name in src/searcher/playwright_searcher.py:319-321, but SiteSelectionAgent.candidates sets them to distinct key and display values in src/agents/research/site_selection.py:50-52.
WatchlistItem.site_name (src/history/watchlist.py:25) is assigned the URL hostname at lines 124 and 134, giving the same field name a third meaning.
detail.suggestion: Standardize on site_id for the stable key and display_name for the human label: rename WebsiteConfig.name to site_id (keep a name input alias for existing YAML), Deal.site_name to site_id, SiteCandidate.name to display_name, and WatchlistItem.site_name to site_host or store the site id there.

..summary: Deal, WatchlistItem and PriceHistoryEntry each name two different record types.

evidence: src/storage/models.py:7 defines Deal with seven fields while src/searcher/adapters/base.py:36 defines a richer Deal; StorageManager actually uses StoredDeal from src/storage/manager.py:16.
src/storage/models.py:30 defines WatchlistItem while src/history/watchlist.py:17 defines a different WatchlistItem with a different field set.

src/storage/models.py is imported only by src/cli/commands/watch.py:118 and a few tests, and its docstring calls itself canonical even though the manager ignores it.
detail.suggestion: Delete the legacy src/storage/models.py and switch watch.py to the canonical Deal/StoredDeal; remove the unused PriceHistoryEntry in src/intelligence/price_tracker.py or rename it to PricePoint. Update the three tests that import src.storage.models.

..summary: DomainProfile.matches() sounds like a predicate but returns an integer score.

evidence: src/output/domains/base.py:46 defines matches(self, folded) -> int and returns 0 or 100-1000+, not a boolean.

..summary: NotificationManager.notify() records a message but sends nothing.

evidence: src/notifications/manager.py:28-35 only consults and updates _seen, then returns True or False; it never calls channel.send() or send_alert().
Its docstring says 'Send a simple deduped notification. Returns True if sent' at line 29, and only tests/test_notifications.py:9-10 calls the method.

..summary: The domain registry exposes a bare get() that is imported and called unqualified as get(domain).

evidence: src/output/domains/registry.py:27 defines get(name) -> DomainProfile and src/output/domains/__init__.py:5-7 re-exports it in __all__.

src/output/processor.py imports get directly and calls get(analysis.domain) at lines 607, 787, 1134, 1151, 1233 and 1734 plus get('computer') at 902, where it reads like a builtin or generic accessor.

detail.suggestion: Rename get to get_domain_profile (or lookup_domain) and update the imports and call sites; keep DOMAIN_REGISTRY for callers that need direct access.

..summary: AgentBase is the base class only for CoordinatorAgent; sibling agents use a different run() contract.

evidence: src/agents/base.py:64 defines AgentBase with abstract execute() returning AgentResult and a run() wrapper that also returns AgentResult.

Only CoordinatorAgent inherits AgentBase (src/agents/coordinator.py:25); DomainExpertAgent, MarketIntelAgent, PriceHunterAgent, QueryExpansionAgent, SiteSelectionAgent, LatestTechTrackerAgent and RecommendationAgent are plain classes whose run() returns dict, for example src/agents/expertise/domain_expert.py:36.
CoordinatorAgent.__init__ annotates agents as list[AgentBase] at src/agents/coordinator.py:28, but it receives those non-subclasses and calls .run() on them at lines 120-177.
detail.suggestion: Either make the seven sibling agents inherit AgentBase and implement execute, or rename AgentBase to CoordinatorBase and type the coordinator's list with a small RunnableAgent Protocol exposing name, role and run(dict) -> dict. Update the re-export and tests to match.

..summary: CLI run paths still thread 15-20 scalar filters; SearchRequest is defined but never used

evidence: SearchRequest is defined at src/searcher/filters.py:542-564, but a repository-wide search finds no reference outside its definition, so the intended grouping never reaches callers.

run() passes 16 positional arguments to run_async (src/cli/app.py:221-244), which forwards them by name to run_search (src/cli/app.py:454-474); run_search declares 20 keyword parameters plus prompt (src/cli/app.py:268-291).

_search_async (src/cli/app.py:882-901) and _diamond_search_async (src/cli/app.py:518-534) repeat the same 15-18 scalar parameter lists, and _resolve_runtime_filters (src/cli/app.py:38-74) builds SearchFilters only at the bottom of the chain.
This is the still-open cli_loose_filter_params issue: the dataclass was added as a partial fix, but the call shape was never migrated.

..summary: MockLLMClient keeps the pre-rename method name and lacks methods the searcher calls

..summary: Data directory site_profiles/ shares its name with site_profiles.py, a latent import shadow

evidence: src/searcher/site_profiles.py:21 sets PROFILE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "site_profiles"; the sibling directory holds 19 YAML profiles and no __init__.py.

Python resolves a regular package before a same-named module, so adding __init__.py to that data directory (a plausible move while the separate mixed-__init__ convention is being fixed) would make `from src.searcher.site_profiles import load_profiles` resolve to the empty package and break profile loading.

setuptools' namespace-package discovery already reports `searcher.site_profiles` as a package (`find_namespace_packages("src")`), so packaging/build tooling sees both the module and a same-named package even though imports currently pick the module.
README.md:691 and :695 document the module and the directory separately, so the distinction exists only in prose, not in the filesystem name.
detail.suggestion: Rename the data directory to an unambiguous name such as src/searcher/profile_data/ and update PROFILE_DIR and the README/script references. Stage it as `git mv src/searcher/site_profiles src/searcher/profile_data`, change site_profiles.py:21, then run `python -m pytest tests/test_site_profiles.py tests/test_discover_helpers.py tests/test_filter_engine.py tests/test_profile_adapter.py -q`; no Python imports change because the YAML is loaded through PROFILE_DIR.

..summary: Selector-health singleton loads a CWD-relative JSON file at import time

evidence: selector_health.py:300 creates `health_tracker = SelectorHealthTracker()` at module scope; `__init__` calls `_load()` (lines 80-110), which opens `data/selector_health.json` before any command runs.

`STORAGE_FILE` is CWD-relative (line 76), so importing `src.cli` reads whichever `data/selector_health.json` sits in the current directory; a probe from a temp CWD loaded that directory's file into the global.
PlaywrightSearcher (line 85) and CLI commands (history.py:242,278,310) each create their own tracker, so multiple in-memory copies can overwrite the same JSON file in one process.

..summary: Price conversion depends on a process-wide rate table set only by load_config()

evidence: currency.py:30-44: `_RATES` is a module-level dict replaced by `set_rates`; the only production caller is `load_config` (config/__init__.py:88-90), so adapters parse prices with DEFAULT_RATES unless config loading ran first.

`parse_price_detail` calls `to_eur(num, code)` without `rates` in the symbol branches (lines 188,193); verified `parse_price_detail('100 Kč', rates={'CZK': 1.0})` returns 2.65 instead of 100.
processor.py:142 reads `currency_rates` from its own config while price parsing reads the global, so the same rate table has two independent sources.

..summary: Dynamic module attributes keep import-time timeout snapshots alive after the refactor

evidence: client.py:46-53 serves `LOCAL_TIMEOUT`, `CLOUD_TIMEOUT`, and `GEMINI_MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS` through module `__getattr__`, but production code always calls `_timeout_from_env`/`_gemini_min_output_tokens`, leaving the names as a compatibility shim with no internal consumers.

..summary: Blanket except ImportError silently disables Diamond Search for real import bugs

evidence: playwright_searcher.py:37-50 wraps imports of eight in-repo agent classes in `try/except ImportError` and sets `DIAMOND_SEARCH_AVAILABLE = False` without logging.

..summary: Monitor inlines five channel registrations and four duplicate try/except blocks

evidence: src/cli/commands/monitor.py:61-89: ConsoleChannel is added directly, then four consecutive try/except blocks import, construct and register System, Email, Webhook and Discord channels.

..summary: discover_site is a 158-line function mixing navigation strategy, capture and status rules

..summary: Inconsistent private-helper naming leaves the doctor command calling a name that does not exist

evidence: src/cli/app.py:815-824: `doctor` calls `asyncio.run(_doctor_async(site, offline))`, but the function is defined as `doctor_async`; there is no `_doctor_async` in the module, so the doctor command raises NameError.

..summary: Monitor constructs ConsoleChannel without the required name, so the command fails before starting

evidence: src/notifications/base.py:31 `def __init__(self, name: str, cooldown_minutes: int = 60)` makes name mandatory.
src/notifications/channels/console.py does not override __init__, but src/cli/commands/monitor.py:65 calls `notif.add_channel(ConsoleChannel())`.

..summary: History CLI calls PriceTracker.get_price_history, which the class does not define

evidence: src/cli/commands/history.py:31 executes `history = tracker.get_price_history(url, days)`.

PriceTracker (src/intelligence/price_tracker.py:63-112) defines record_sighting, get_price_trend_for_deal, get_deals_nearing_target and get_deals_below_price only; `hasattr(PriceTracker, 'get_price_history')` is False.

..summary: parse_price/parse_price_detail accept a rates override but ignore it when a currency symbol is present

evidence: src/searcher/currency.py:188 and 193 call `to_eur(num, code)` in the currency-symbol branch; only the no-symbol fallback at line 200 passes `rates`.
The docstring says conversion uses the supplied rates, and `to_eur(amount, currency, rates)` supports it, so the public parameter is silently dropped.
Verified: `parse_price_detail('1000 Kc', rates={'CZK': 1.0})` returns `(1000.0, 26.5, 'CZK')` instead of 1000.0 EUR.

..summary: BrowserManager's CDP detection and close() behavior contradict their names and docstrings

evidence: src/browser/manager.py:169-172 `_is_cdp_connected()` returns `context.browser.is_connected()`, which is true for regular and persistent contexts too; consequently `get_page()` skips fingerprint rotation on every normal path, not just CDP.
src/browser/manager.py:212-218 says 'Only disconnect... without killing a CDP-attached browser' but closes `self._browser`, which `get_browser()` assigned to the CDP BrowserContext at line 57.
The comment directly above the call warns that closing the context would close the user's own tabs, so the implementation contradicts the documented safety guarantee.
detail.suggestion: Track the CDP connection explicitly (store the CDP Browser/context and a boolean) and use that for fingerprint gating; on close, disconnect/close the CDP browser connection without calling close() on the user's context.

..summary: AlertRule.condition uses the builtin callable as a type annotation and channels contradicts its default

evidence: src/notifications/rules.py:13 `condition: callable` uses the builtin function, not a type; mypy reports `Function "builtins.callable" is not valid as a type`.
Line 16 `channels: list[str] = None` declares a non-optional list but defaults to None.
Line 20 invokes `self.condition(context)`, so the field is really `Callable[[dict], bool]`.
detail.suggestion: Import Callable from collections.abc, annotate `condition: Callable[[dict], bool]`, and make `channels: list[str] | None = None` (or default_factory=list if an empty list is intended).

..summary: Shared models and constructors declare non-optional types while defaulting to None

evidence: src/config/models.py:75 `local_coordination: LocalCoordinationConfig = None`; consumers compensate with `getattr(..., None)` at src/llm/client.py:210.
src/notifications/base.py:19 `metadata: dict = None` is normalized in __post_init__, but the declared field type rejects None.

src/notifications/channels/webhook.py:15 `headers: dict = None`, src/history/watchlist.py:47 `storage: StorageManager = None, notifications: NotificationManager = None`, and src/agents/coordinator.py:28 `config: dict = None` are all implicit Optionals under PEP 484.
Each site forces a reader to inspect the body (or rely on getattr) to learn that None is an accepted value.
detail.suggestion: Annotate every optional parameter/field as `X | None` and use Field(default_factory=...) for mutable collections; add mypy to CI so new implicit Optionals are rejected.

..summary: Watchlist add passes --threshold into site_name and does not persist updates to existing items

evidence: add_item signature at src/history/watchlist.py:104-113 is `(url, title, target_price_eur, condition, category, site_name='', alert_threshold_pct=5.0)`.

src/cli/commands/history.py:126 calls `add_item(url, title, target_price, condition, category, threshold)`, so threshold becomes site_name and alert_threshold_pct stays 5.0 while the command echoes the user's threshold.
In the existing-item branch (watchlist.py:118-126) the method mutates fields and returns without calling `_save()`, so the update is lost when the process exits.
detail.suggestion: Call add_item with keyword arguments (`site_name=...`, `alert_threshold_pct=threshold`) and call `_save()` before returning from the existing-item branch; cover the update path with a test.

..summary: `doctor` command calls undefined `_doctor_async`, so every invocation raises NameError

evidence: src/cli/app.py:821 runs `asyncio.run(_doctor_async(site, offline))`.
The only implementation is `async def doctor_async(...)` at src/cli/app.py:824; no `_doctor_async` symbol is defined or imported anywhere in the repository.
src/cli/commands/doctor.py:11 imports and calls `doctor_async`, confirming which name was intended.
detail.suggestion: Call `doctor_async(site, offline)` in the command (or rename the function to `_doctor_async` and update the wrapper), then add a CLI smoke test that invokes each registered command.

..summary: `monitor` crashes at startup because `ConsoleChannel()` is missing its required `name` argument

evidence: NotificationChannel.__init__(name, cooldown_minutes=60) requires `name` (src/notifications/base.py:31), and ConsoleChannel (src/notifications/channels/console.py:10) does not override `__init__`.
src/cli/commands/monitor.py:65 calls `notif.add_channel(ConsoleChannel())` before the run loop, which raises `TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'name'`.

The same block calls `WebhookChannel(ch.name)` and `DiscordChannel(ch.name)` without the required `url`/`webhook_url`; those TypeErrors are caught by the surrounding `except Exception`, so webhook and Discord channels are silently never added (config models expose URLs under `ch.settings`).
detail.suggestion: Pass an explicit channel name (`ConsoleChannel("console")`) and build the configured channels with their settings (`WebhookChannel(ch.name, ch.settings["url"])`, `DiscordChannel(ch.name, ch.settings["webhook_url"])`); do not swallow constructor TypeError in the capability probe.

..summary: `watchlist add` passes the alert threshold into the `site_name` parameter, silently disabling the threshold

evidence: WatchlistManager.add_item signature is `(self, url, title, target_price_eur, condition='any', category='any', site_name='', alert_threshold_pct=5.0)` (src/history/watchlist.py:104-113).
src/cli/commands/history.py:126 calls `add_item(url, title, target_price, condition, category, threshold)` with six positionals, so `threshold` binds to `site_name`.
add_item then overwrites `site_name` with the URL host (line 124) and leaves `alert_threshold_pct` at its 5.0 default.
detail.suggestion: Pass the value by keyword: `wl_manager.add_item(url, title, target_price, condition, category, alert_threshold_pct=threshold)`, or pass `site_name` explicitly before it.

..summary: Watchlist price alerts can never fire: `_search_item` always returns [] and `_send_alert` reads a nonexistent `Deal.url_hash`

evidence: src/history/watchlist.py:223-227 defines `_search_item` as a comment plus `return []`, so `check_prices` hits `if not deals: continue` for every item.
`check_prices` initializes `alerts = []` (line 161) but never appends to it and returns `[]` at line 221; the CLI exposes this as `watchlist check-async` (src/cli/commands/history.py:159-183).
`_send_alert` builds an alert dict and only logs it, indexing `self.items[deal.url_hash]` at lines 256-267 even though `Deal` (src/searcher/adapters/base.py:35-48) has no `url_hash` attribute.
The alert text computes the drop as `(last_price - price) / price` while `check_prices` computes `(previous_price - price) / previous_price`, so the two percentages would disagree if the path ran.
detail.suggestion: Either implement `_search_item` against PlaywrightSearcher and key the alert by the passed `WatchlistItem`, or remove the check/check-async actions until it is implemented; use the already-computed `drop_pct` in `_send_alert` instead of recomputing it from a different denominator.

..summary: `watch` report raises KeyError when a URL fetch fails because the error result omits `stock`

evidence: `_fetch_product` returns `{"url": url, "title": "", "price": None, "error": str(exc)}` on navigation failure (src/cli/commands/watch.py:29), with no `stock` key.
The report loop at line 135 unconditionally reads `r['stock']`, so one unreachable URL aborts report generation after all pages were already fetched.
detail.suggestion: Return `"stock": "unknown"` from the error path, or use `r.get("stock", "unknown")` in the report.

..summary: Selector health decay's 72-hour branch is unreachable, so very stale selectors keep the 0.5 multiplier

evidence: SelectorMetric.health_score uses `if hours_since > 24: rate *= 0.5; elif hours_since > 72: rate *= 0.25` (lines 41-46).
Every value greater than 72 also satisfies greater than 24, so the 0.25 branch can never execute.
detail.suggestion: Order the checks from most to least severe: `if hours_since > 72: rate *= 0.25 elif hours_since > 24: rate *= 0.5`.

..summary: `has_significant_changes` ignores `threshold_pct`, and the monitor's `--price-drop-threshold` never reaches it

evidence: RunChangeReport.has_significant_changes(threshold_pct=10.0) returns true whenever any price change, new deal or removed deal exists; `threshold_pct` is never read (src/intelligence/change_detector.py:47-53).
A 0.01% price movement therefore counts as significant at the default 10% threshold; condition_changes and availability_changes are not considered at all.
src/cli/commands/monitor.py:44 accepts `price_drop_threshold` but never uses it, and line 127 calls `generate_run_report(run_id, prompt, deals, previous_run_id)` without a threshold.
detail.suggestion: Filter `price_changes` by `abs(change_pct) >= threshold_pct`, include condition and availability counts in the verdict, and pass `price_drop_threshold` through `generate_run_report` to `has_significant_changes` before sending the monitor alert.

..summary: `parse_price_detail` ignores its `rates` argument whenever the text contains a currency symbol

evidence: The currency-symbol branch calls `to_eur(num, code)` at lines 188 and 193 without passing `rates`; the no-symbol fallback passes `rates` at line 200.

With a CZK override of 0.5, `parse_price_detail('1000 Kc', 'EUR', {'CZK': 0.5})` returns `(1000.0, 26.5, 'CZK')`, while `parse_price_detail('1000', 'CZK', {'CZK': 0.5})` returns 500.0 EUR; configured rates therefore apply only to bare numbers.
The same function re-imports `re` inside the loop (line 180) although `re` is already imported at module level.
detail.suggestion: Pass `rates` to both symbol-path `to_eur` calls and remove the inner `import re`.

..summary: `BrowserManager.close()` closes the CDP-borrowed context because `_browser` aliases `_context`

evidence: On the CDP path `_create_browser` returns `self._context` (line 79), and `get_browser` stores that return value in `self._browser` (line 57).

`close()` sees `_cdp_connected` and calls `await self._browser.close()` (lines 214-218), which closes the user's borrowed BrowserContext even though the adjacent comment says only a disconnect is allowed.
On the non-CDP persistent path `_browser` and `_context` are also the same object, so `close()` calls `close()` twice (lines 220-223).
detail.suggestion: Keep the CDP `Browser` handle separate from `_context`; in CDP mode drop the references and `stop()` Playwright without closing the context, while still closing contexts this manager created itself.

..summary: `NotificationManager.notify` never sends through a channel but reports success

evidence: notify() only reads and updates `_seen` and returns True/False for the cooldown decision (src/notifications/manager.py:28-35); `self.channels` is never touched.
It is declared `async` but contains no `await`, so it is a synchronous dedupe check wrapped in an async API.
The constructor accepts `rate_limit` and stores `_send_timestamps`, but neither is ever read, and tests/test_notifications.py:9-10 only asserts the dedupe booleans, cementing the no-op contract.
detail.suggestion: Either await `channel.send` for the selected channels (mirroring `send_alert`) and enforce the rate limit, or rename the method to `should_notify` and make it synchronous so the signature and docstring match its behavior.

..summary: CLI command ownership is split between src/cli/app.py and src/cli/commands/ with no consistent rule.

evidence: app.py is 1017 lines and registers 17 commands; 15 command bodies (ask, run, search, diamond-search, doctor, sites, browsers, login-sites, ...) live there, while commands/ has only three modules.
app.py's monitor and watch are thin Typer wrappers that forward to commands.monitor.monitor and commands.watch.watch, so those commands have two definitions in two files.
Selector-health is exposed twice: the top-level selector-health command in app.py:594 and the history selector health|unhealthy|clear group in commands/history.py:221-327.
src/cli/main.py duplicates src/cli/__main__.py and src/__main__.py and is referenced only by tests/test_fixpass.py.
detail.suggestion: Choose one rule and apply it: move every command body into src/cli/commands/<name>.py (history already models the pattern) and leave app.py for registration and shared helpers, or delete commands/ and keep app.py. Remove the duplicate selector-health surface and the unused src/cli/main.py entry point.

..summary: search and diamond-search reimplement the run_search cycle, so run/search/diamond-search diverge.

evidence: run and ask call run_search (app.py:268), which owns config overrides, filter resolution, storage, search, pruning and ResultProcessor.save_results.
search calls _search_async (app.py:882), which re-implements filter resolution, storage, search and save but does not apply the --format/--domain overrides and constructs ResultProcessor differently.
diamond_search calls _diamond_search_async (app.py:518), a third copy that resolves filters, builds storage/browser/processor and calls search_with_diamond.
tests/test_cli_flags.py monkeypatches run_async, _search_async and _diamond_search_async, so the three-entry-point shape is now part of the test contract.
detail.suggestion: Make run_search the only cycle: add a search_mode/search_fn parameter for standard vs Diamond and a save/render option for commands that print progress, then have run, ask, search and diamond_search delegate to it. Delete _search_async and _diamond_search_async and update the wiring test.

..summary: Price trend, drop and new-low analytics have four owners and duplicated thresholds.

evidence: StorageManager.detect_price_drops (threshold 5.0), detect_new_lows and get_price_trend implement SQL/grouping that TrendsAnalyzer.get_price_drops (threshold 10.0), get_new_lows and analyze_category duplicate.

WatchlistManager.get_price_trend (line 294) computes its own +/-5% trend from price_history with an unused cutoff local; PriceTracker.get_price_trend_for_deal just delegates to StorageManager.get_price_trend.
The storage-level detect_* methods are exercised only by tests (test_fixpass.py, test_storage_persistence.py), while the CLI history trends path uses TrendsAnalyzer.
detail.suggestion: Pick one analytics owner (e.g. TrendsAnalyzer, with PriceTracker delegating to it), move the shared SQL/threshold logic there, and delete StorageManager.detect_price_drops/detect_new_lows/get_price_trend plus WatchlistManager.get_price_trend. Define one trend-threshold constant instead of the 5.0/10.0 copies.

..summary: Two 'research' packages and two site-selection implementations obscure which component owns either.

evidence: src/research/ holds external web search and domain discovery; src/agents/research/ holds the Diamond research agents. Both are named research and only the agent package appears in the README tree.

src/searcher/site_selection.py owns the real selection (SiteSelector.select, called at playwright_searcher.py:343), while src/agents/research/site_selection.py defines a second SiteSelectionAgent that is only wired into the Diamond coordinator (playwright_searcher.py:101).

detail.suggestion: Give site selection one owner: have SiteSelectionAgent delegate to SiteSelector.select and return its result, or remove the agent and keep the selector. Rename src/research/ to a name that says web search/discovery (e.g. src/web_research/) and document the distinction from agents/research/ in the README.

..summary: ResultProcessor owns deal analysis, ranking and four export formats in one 1904-line class.

evidence: ResultProcessor.save_results (line 241) is documented as "Write one JSON file and one Markdown file" but also writes CSV and XLSX and runs deduplication, brand filtering, LLM analysis, outlier filtering and winner selection.

The class has 41 methods and 1904 lines, mixing scoring (_weighted_score, _score_breakdown), cross-site linking (_add_cross_alternatives), price formatting and Markdown rendering (_deal_card, _to_markdown, _checklist).
src/output/__init__.py exports nothing, so every consumer imports processor.py directly and the package's public surface is effectively the god module.
detail.suggestion: Split ResultProcessor into an analysis/scoring module and renderer modules (Markdown, JSON, CSV, XLSX), leaving save_results as thin orchestration. Update the docstring to name all outputs and re-export the intended public types from src/output/__init__.py.

..summary: load_config parse and validation errors are uncaught, so config-check and every command traceback on bad config

evidence: config/__init__.py:80-84 performs open(config_path), yaml.safe_load(resolve_env_placeholders(raw)) and AppConfig(**config_data) with no exception boundary; resolve_env_placeholders (63-65) raises ValueError for a missing environment variable.
Manual check: a malformed YAML file raised yaml.parser.ParserError straight out of load_config, so callers receive the parser's multi-line traceback text rather than a domain error.
config_check (app.py:758-761), whose docstring says it validates config.yaml, calls load_config with no handler; run, search, diamond_search, monitor and doctor do the same.
detail.suggestion: Catch (OSError, yaml.YAMLError, ValueError, pydantic.ValidationError) in load_config or a shared CLI wrapper, print Error: invalid config <path>: <first error> and exit 1, and make config-check report the validation failure instead of tracebacking.

..summary: Adapters turn navigation and timeout failures into empty lists, so outages look like zero-deal searches

evidence: alza.py:40-54, amazon.py:53-56, backmarket.py:39-41, facebook.py:43-45 and ebay.py:90-97 catch PlaywrightError around _goto_search and selector waits, log at debug and return [].

playwright_searcher.py:718-721 records bool(deals) as the success flag; SelectorHealthTracker.record_search_result (selector_health.py:133-141) has no failure-reason field, so DNS errors, navigation timeouts and a genuine no-match page all look identical.
Adapter failures log at debug and logging is only configured at DEBUG when --debug is passed (app.py:122,135,220,302,432), so a normal run reports zero deals with no visible cause.
detail.suggestion: Return a per-site outcome (deals plus failure_reason) or raise a SiteUnavailableError from navigation/timeout paths, reserving an empty list for a loaded page with no matching cards. Record the reason in _skipped_sites and health, and add adapter plus searcher tests that simulate PlaywrightError.

..summary: Diamond agents look for llm.chat(), which LLMClient does not expose, so every agent silently uses its deterministic fallback.

evidence: src/agents/llm_support.py:32 resolves the model with getattr(self.llm, 'chat', None) and returns None when absent.
src/llm/client.py exposes chat_json() and private _chat(), but no public chat(); the only class with chat() is the FakeLLM in tests/test_agents_llm.py.
src/agents/research/query_expansion.py:39 still reports source='llm' whenever self.llm is not None, even though _ask() never reached it.
detail.suggestion: Add async def chat(self, system, user, max_tokens=400) to LLMClient delegating to _chat, or make LLMBackedAgent._ask call chat_json/_chat directly; then add an agent test that wires the real LLMClient with a mocked transport instead of only FakeLLM.

..summary: Coordinator wraps PriceHunter output under 'price_hunter', but RecommendationAgent reads price.enriched_deals, so synthesis always reports no deals.

evidence: src/agents/coordinator.py:169 returns {'price_hunter': _extract_result(result)}.
src/agents/coordinator.py:200-203 passes that wrapper as all_results['price'] into _synthesize_results.
src/agents/synthesis/recommendation.py:31-32 reads all_results['price'].get('enriched_deals', []) and best_overall, so best_overall is always None and status becomes no_deals_found.
tests/test_agent_pipeline.py tests RecommendationAgent with the unwrapped shape, so the coordinator handoff is untested.
detail.suggestion: Return the PriceHunter payload directly from _run_price_layer (or unwrap price_hunter in _synthesize_results), and add a CoordinatorAgent end-to-end test asserting final_recommendation.status == 'success' when deals are supplied.

..summary: Diamond site selection and expert scores are computed but never used by the actual search or the saved report.

evidence: src/searcher/playwright_searcher.py:804-814 extracts only research['query_expansion']['expanded_queries'] and calls self.search(), which runs its own _select_sites; SiteSelectionAgent.run's selected_sites is dropped.
src/searcher/playwright_searcher.py:820-826 attaches expert_score/expert_analysis as dynamic Deal attributes.
src/output/processor.py:1348-1386 never serializes expert_score/expert_analysis, and _diamond_search_async builds ResultProcessor without an LLM, so the report ranks by its own heuristic.
The only surface for expert_score is the console loop in src/cli/app.py:586-590.
detail.suggestion: Either wire the Diamond outputs through: pass research['site_selection']['selected_sites'] as sites= to self.search and add expert_score/expert_analysis to DealAnalysis/_deal_to_dict; or delete the duplicate post-search scoring and unused site-selection agent so there is one ranking path.

..summary: Four CLI paths rebuild the same search cycle with different omissions, so behavior and reporting drift by command.

evidence: run_search (src/cli/app.py:268-405) resolves filters, searches, prunes, saves deals and passes site_plan; _search_async (882-959) repeats the sequence but never calls prune_missing and exposes --max-pages/--headless that it never uses.
_diamond_search_async (src/cli/app.py:518-591) builds ResultProcessor without an LLM and does not pass site_plan, while run_search and _search_async both do.
_monitor_async (src/cli/commands/monitor.py:108-165) repeats config/LLM/storage/browser/search/save and owns its own loop and notification setup.
_watch_async (src/cli/commands/watch.py:157-186) repeats LLM/BrowserManager/PlaywrightSearcher setup for alternatives.
detail.suggestion: Make run_search the single search-cycle entry point: have the search command delegate to it (adding the domain/output override), have monitor call it per iteration, and remove or plumb the unused max_pages/headless parameters; keep watch's alternatives call as a small helper.

..summary: Trend and change-detection modules query storage.db directly, and the report layer opens its own StorageManager, so schema knowledge leaks across layers.

evidence: src/history/trends.py:33, 116, 129, 184 and 211 run hand-written SQL against self.storage.db.
src/intelligence/change_detector.py:252-260 joins price_history and deals through self.storage.db.execute.
src/output/processor.py:1595-1597 constructs a second StorageManager inside _price_history_lines just to render price history.
StorageManager already owns the connection and schema, so callers now depend on column names and join details.
detail.suggestion: Add read methods to StorageManager (for example get_category_price_rows, get_category_counts and get_run_price_rows) and pass the same StorageManager into ResultProcessor; delete the raw SQL from analytics and report modules.

..summary: Storage reads availability/seller/shipping attributes that Deal never declares, and records the wrong original price.

evidence: Deal (src/searcher/adapters/base.py:35-48) declares original_price but not availability, seller_name, seller_rating or shipping_cost_eur; save_deal (src/storage/manager.py:120,135-138) reads all four via getattr defaults.

record_price_sighting (src/storage/manager.py:205) reads getattr(deal, 'original_price_eur', deal.price_eur), so Deal.original_price is ignored and the original-price column always equals the EUR price.
detail.suggestion: Declare the four persisted fields on Deal (or add one explicit Deal-to-row mapper in storage) and use deal.original_price for original_price_eur; add a storage test that saves an adapter Deal and asserts the original/seller fields survive.

..summary: watchlist check and check-async advertise price monitoring but never search, notify or return results.

evidence: src/history/watchlist.py:226-230 _search_item always returns [] with a placeholder comment; check_prices therefore skips every item and returns [] (lines 164-224).
src/history/watchlist.py:252-275 _send_alert only logs and would index deal.url_hash and self.items[deal.url_hash], but Deal has no url_hash attribute.
src/cli/commands/history.py:162-190: the 'check' action only prints an instruction, and 'check-async' builds unused BrowserManager/MockLLM instances before calling the no-op.
detail.suggestion: Either implement _search_item by delegating to PlaywrightSearcher.search(item.title, ...) and send Alert objects through NotificationManager, or delete check_prices/check-async and the 'check' action so the CLI stops advertising a no-op.

..summary: The watch command launches its own Chromium and parses prices with local regexes instead of using BrowserManager and the adapter/price layer.

evidence: src/cli/commands/watch.py:113-115 uses async_playwright() and pw.chromium.launch() directly, bypassing BrowserManager's CDP/persistent-profile/fingerprint setup.

src/cli/commands/watch.py:26-103 reimplements title/price/stock extraction with local selector lists and number parsing, duplicating BaseAdapter.parse_price_with_currency (src/searcher/adapters/base.py:183).
src/cli/commands/watch.py:124-128 constructs a Deal with condition='any' and site_name='watchlist', so the saved sighting cannot participate in normal site/condition reporting.
detail.suggestion: Use BrowserManager.get_page() and BaseAdapter.parse_price_with_currency (or add a small fetch_detail method on BaseAdapter) to build the Deal; keep direct-URL fetching in the adapter layer rather than in the CLI command.

..summary: Watchlist price checking is untested and ships with a no-op searcher and undelivered alerts

evidence: `WatchlistManager.check_prices` (src/history/watchlist.py:164) is reachable from `history watchlist --check` (src/cli/commands/history.py:185), but tests/test_watchlist.py only covers add_item/get_item persistence and CLI argument plumbing; no test calls check_prices.

The unexecuted lines are exactly the price-drop, target-reached and alert branches (lines 166-224), so the feature's core promise has never been validated by a test.
detail.suggestion: Add a tests/test_watchlist.py case that injects a fake searcher returning one Deal and a fake NotificationChannel; assert check_prices updates current_price_eur/price_history and sends a drop alert at alert_threshold_pct. Thread the `searcher` argument into `_search_item` and dispatch the built alert through `self.notifications.send_alert` so the test exercises the real path.

..summary: Browser manager, monitor/watch CLI and scheduler are 6-21% covered

evidence: Fresh `pytest --cov=src` reports src/browser/manager.py 21%, src/cli/commands/watch.py 6%, src/cli/commands/history.py 14%, src/cli/commands/monitor.py 15% and src/scheduler/tasks.py 14%, against 66% overall.

The monitor loop is the product's scheduled path, yet `monitor` (109 statements) and `watch` (162 statements) have no behavioural test file.

..summary: Several tests can never fail: source-text substrings and conditional tautologies

evidence: tests/test_fixpass.py:7-10 asserts the literal string `ph.url = d.url` appears in `inspect.getsource(StorageManager.detect_price_drops)`; a rename or formatting change breaks the test while a broken join can still pass.

tests/test_selector_health_log.py:39 evaluates `events[0]["deals_found"] if "deals_found" in events[0] else True`; tests/test_migrations.py:79 (`... if hasattr(saved, "currency") else True`) and tests/test_browser_registry.py:56 (`... is False or True`) use the same pass-when-absent shape.

tests/test_browser_registry.py:52-59 is named 'resolve_missing_browser_raises_with_paths' but never asserts that the error names the searched paths; it repeats the unknown-browser check from the previous test.

..summary: The 663-test suite is never run by CI and coverage has no threshold

evidence: .github/ contains CODEOWNERS, Dependabot and issue templates but no workflows directory; there is no tox.ini, noxfile.py, Makefile or pre-commit configuration in the repo root.

..summary: `doctor` calls undefined `_doctor_async`, so the command raises NameError before diagnostics run.

evidence: src/cli/app.py:821 calls `asyncio.run(_doctor_async(site, offline))`.
The only implementation is `async def doctor_async(...)` at src/cli/app.py:824; no `_doctor_async` symbol exists in src/ or tests/.

..summary: `WatchlistManager.check_prices` ignores its `searcher`/`llm` arguments and always returns an empty list.

evidence: src/history/watchlist.py:164 declares `async def check_prices(self, searcher, llm)` but never references either parameter.
src/history/watchlist.py:226-230 `_search_item` is a stub containing `# For now, return empty list` and `return []`, so every item is skipped at line 174.
The method returns `[]` at line 224 even when items were attempted, and per-item exceptions are logged then swallowed by the enclosing `except Exception`.
detail.suggestion: Implement `_search_item` to call the supplied searcher (or inject a search callable), return real deals, and surface failures; if the feature is not ready, remove `check_prices` and the CLI action instead of exposing a no-op.

..summary: LLM access is duck-typed: no public `chat`, private `_chat` leaks, and `MockLLMClient` omits half the surface.

evidence: src/llm/client.py defines `_chat` at line 359 and `chat_json` at line 242, but no public `chat` method.
src/agents/llm_support.py:32-35 does `getattr(self.llm, 'chat', None)` and returns None when absent, so `QueryExpansionAgent._ask_json` always falls back to templates even with a real LLMClient.
src/output/processor.py:666 and :1418 call `self.llm._chat`; src/searcher/query_language.py:113 calls `llm._chat`.

src/llm/mock_client.py implements the query ladder but omits `chat`, `chat_json`, `extract_search_filters` and `classify_price_quotes`; call sites probe with `hasattr`/`getattr` and silently disable those paths.
detail.suggestion: Add a public `async chat(system, user, max_tokens, temperature)` wrapper to `LLMClient`, migrate the processor and query translator to it, and give `MockLLMClient` the same public methods (or define a small Protocol both satisfy); keep `_chat` private.

..summary: `_chat` returns the user prompt when every provider fails, so callers parse instruction text as model output.

evidence: src/llm/client.py:429-431 logs `All LLM providers failed` and then does `return user`.

`judge_results` (src/llm/client.py:611-622) regexes `KEEP|DISCARD` from the reply; the user prompt itself contains `One KEEP/DISCARD line per item`, so a failed call produces two verdicts and keeps only the first deal instead of taking the `parsed_lines == 0` keep-all fallback.
`localise_query` (src/searcher/query_language.py:112-129) treats that echoed instruction as a translation and caches it for the target language.
detail.suggestion: Return an empty string or raise a typed `LLMUnavailableError` on total failure; keep the keyword-query fallback in `generate_search_query_async`, make `judge_results`/`rank_results` check for empty output, and have `localise_query` return the original query. Add a no-provider regression test.

..summary: CLI search pipeline duplicates 18-21 parameter signatures; `SearchRequest` is unused and `search` flags are ignored.

evidence: `run` (src/cli/app.py:195), `run_search` (:268), `run_async` (:408) and `search` (:837) each redeclare the same filter/output/network options; `run` forwards them positionally to `run_async`, which forwards keywords to `run_search`.
`SearchRequest` (src/searcher/filters.py:562) groups exactly those fields but has no references in src/ or tests/.
`search` advertises `--max-pages` and `--headless` (:843-844); `_search_async` (:882-959) never reads either parameter.
`tests/test_cli_flags.py:35` asserts `captured["args"][-2:] == ("cz", 3)`, locking the fragile positional order.
detail.suggestion: Have the Typer callbacks build a `SearchRequest` and pass it to one `run_search(request)`; delete `run_async`'s duplicate parameter list; either wire `max_pages`/`headless` into config or remove those flags; assert request fields rather than argument positions in tests.

..summary: `BrowserManager.get_browser` returns either a `Browser` or a `BrowserContext`, so callers cannot rely on the type.

evidence: src/browser/manager.py:53 annotates `async def get_browser(self) -> Browser | BrowserContext`.
The CDP and persistent-context paths return `self._context` (:79 and :113), while the last-resort path returns the context at :132; `self._browser` remains the underlying browser.
`get_page` (:156) calls `browser.new_page()` on the union, which only works because both Playwright types happen to expose `new_page`.
`PlaywrightSearcher` stores the result as `self.browser: BrowserContext | None` (:75), contradicting the declared union.
detail.suggestion: Split the API into `get_context() -> BrowserContext` (creating or attaching as needed) and a private `_get_browser()`; have `get_page` and `PlaywrightSearcher` depend on the context instead of a union.

..summary: Canonical StrEnums are bypassed by raw-string fields from Deal through storage, adapters and searcher signatures

evidence: Deal.condition: str = 'unknown' and Deal.category: str = 'general' (adapters/base.py:44-45) while Condition/Category StrEnums exist in config/models.py:9-25.

BaseAdapter.supported_conditions/supported_categories are ClassVar[list[str]] (adapters/base.py:71-72) and every concrete adapter repeats raw literals (alza.py:24-25, bazos.py:23-24, ebay.py:32-33, facebook.py:20-21, backmarket.py:22-23, amazon.py:24-31).
StoredDeal.condition/category/price_kind are str (storage/manager.py:19-20,32); price_kind is persisted as quote.kind.value (manager.py:142) and read back as an untyped string.

SiteSpec.categories/conditions are tuple[str, ...] and status is str (site_registry.py:27-29); SiteCandidate.status is str (site_selection.py:41); PlaywrightSearcher.search annotates condition/category as str while defaulting to Condition.ANY/Category.ANY (playwright_searcher.py:377-378).
SearchFilters.condition is correctly Condition | None (filters.py:250), proving the enum path works; the type is then dropped at the next call boundary.
detail.suggestion: Finish the migration: add explicit UNKNOWN members where needed and type Deal.condition/category with Condition/Category, adapter capability lists as tuple[Condition, ...]/tuple[Category, ...], StoredDeal.price_kind as PriceKind, and PlaywrightSearcher/PriceTracker/StorageManager signatures with the enums; convert to str only at YAML/JSON/DB edges.

..summary: 43 public functions and methods lack return annotations, concentrated in CLI, agents, browser and notifications

evidence: AST scan: 30 module-level public functions have no return annotation, including all Typer commands in cli/app.py (ask, run, search, diamond_search, doctor, monitor, watch, ...) and cli/commands/history.py:21,57,104,225,283,299.

13 public methods are unannotated, e.g. LLMClient.chat_json (llm/client.py:244), BasePage.goto/wait_for_load (browser/pom/base.py:14,18), NotificationManager.add_channel/add_rule/send_alert (notifications/manager.py:22,25,37), SelectorHealthTracker.record_search_result (diagnostics/selector_health.py:133).
mypy --disallow-untyped-defs reports 142 no-untyped-def errors across 58 files; a further 142 type-arg errors show bare dict/list/tuple annotations instead of parameters.
The current gate (mypy default with check_untyped_defs) passes, so these gaps are invisible to CI rather than known-safe.
detail.suggestion: Annotate the Typer commands with '-> None', then the high-traffic methods (chat_json -> dict[str, Any] | list[Any] | None, BasePage.goto -> None, sender methods -> bool/None); replace bare dict/list/tuple with parameterized types and enable disallow_untyped_defs package-by-package to ratchet.

..summary: Code reads Deal attributes that the dataclass never declares, so missing fields default silently and alerts crash

evidence: Deal (adapters/base.py:37-52) defines no availability, seller_name, seller_rating, shipping_cost_eur or effective_price_eur, but save_deal/record_price_sighting read them via getattr(..., default) at storage/manager.py:120,135-137,205,208-211.

No adapter in src assigns deal.availability/seller_name/seller_rating/shipping_cost_eur, so the DB columns are always 'unknown'/''/0.0 even though profile_adapter scrapes seller/shipping into metadata.

record_price_sighting reads getattr(deal, 'original_price_eur', deal.price_eur) (manager.py:205) although the field is Deal.original_price (adapters/base.py:48), so price history loses the pre-conversion amount.
_effective_price uses getattr(deal, 'effective_price_eur', 0.0) (price_tracker.py:12) although Deal exposes the comparable_price_eur property (adapters/base.py:54-59).
WatchlistManager._send_alert reads deal.url_hash (watchlist.py:260-271), a field Deal does not define, so every price-drop alert raises AttributeError inside the broad except at watchlist.py:222.
detail.suggestion: Declare the optional attributes on Deal (or delete the unused DB columns and read seller/availability from metadata on purpose), replace the string getattr calls with Deal.original_price/comparable_price_eur, and type _send_alert(self, item: WatchlistItem, deal: Deal, drop_pct: float) -> None using item.url_hash.

..summary: Deal.metadata is a bare dict with divergent adapter keys and a second JSON-string representation in storage

evidence: Deal.metadata is declared as plain 'dict' (adapters/base.py:47), while StoredDeal.metadata is a JSON string (storage/manager.py:30), so the same concept changes type across the persistence boundary.

Adapter key sets diverge: alza writes code/description/rating/reviews, ebay writes subtitle, bazos writes detail_failed/detail_skipped/location, profile_adapter writes arbitrary extraction fields plus image, and dedup writes duplicates.
FilterEngine._matches reads brand/location/seller/seller_type/shipping with .get() and re-wraps non-dicts (filter_engine.py:210-241), which is exactly the distrust a TypedDict would make unnecessary.
The values are heterogeneous (str, bool, float, list, dict), so 'dict' gives callers no key or value contract.
detail.suggestion: Define DealMetadata(TypedDict, total=False) for the shared keys (brand, location, seller, seller_type, shipping, card_text, original_price, detail_failed, detail_skipped, duplicates) and fall back to dict[str, object] for adapter-specific keys; serialize to JSON only inside storage with a single helper.

..summary: PriceHistoryEntry exists twice with diverging fields and is unused while analytics return untyped dicts

evidence: storage/manager.py:36-51 defines PriceHistoryEntry with effective_price_eur and price_kind; intelligence/price_tracker.py:16-29 defines the same name without those two fields.
Neither PriceHistoryEntry is imported or constructed anywhere in src, scripts or tests.
PriceDropAlert, NewLowAlert, PriceTrend (price_tracker.py:32-60) and CategoryTrend (history/trends.py:9-19) are also unreferenced.

StorageManager.get_price_history returns list[dict] (manager.py:225) and get_price_trend returns dict (manager.py:315), so CLI/report code indexes string keys with no field names or nullability contract.
detail.suggestion: Keep one price-history record type (dataclass or TypedDict) covering every persisted column, return it from StorageManager and PriceTracker, and delete the unused alert/trend dataclasses or make them the actual return types.

..summary: Coordinator mirrors Deal dataclasses into hand-written dicts, dropping typed fields before agents score them

evidence: CoordinatorAgent.score_deals(self, prompt, research, deals, run_id) has no parameter annotations (coordinator.py:186-188) and builds deal_dicts with only url/title/price_eur/condition/category/site_name/metadata (coordinator.py:194-201).
Deal.price_quote, original_price, original_currency, expert_score and expert_analysis (adapters/base.py:48-52) are silently dropped by that projection.
Agents then mutate untyped dicts: DomainExpertAgent.run does deal.setdefault('metadata', {}) and deal['expert_score'] = ... (domain_expert.py:47-56), and _score_deal(deal) is unannotated.
The projection is a second, unchecked definition of the Deal shape that will not be updated when Deal grows.
detail.suggestion: Type score_deals to accept list[Deal], convert once with dataclasses.asdict() or a single DealPayload TypedDict, and annotate the agents' input (e.g. AgentInput TypedDict) so omitted fields fail type checking rather than disappearing at runtime.

..summary: Site status is an unconstrained string with a comment-defined vocabulary despite the Literal pattern elsewhere

evidence: SiteSpec.status: str with '# working | blocked | needs_login | planned' at site_registry.py:29; the real vocabulary exists only in the module docstring (site_registry.py:9-13).
by_status(status: str) accepts any string and returns [] on a typo (site_registry.py:337-338); summary() keys a dict[str, int] by arbitrary status strings (site_registry.py:341-344).
SiteCandidate.status defaults to the literal 'planned' with the same str annotation (site_selection.py:41).
site_profiles.py:23 already defines ProfileStatus = Literal[...] for the adjacent lifecycle, so the pattern is established but was not applied to SiteSpec.
detail.suggestion: Define SiteStatus = Literal['working', 'blocked', 'needs_login', 'planned'] (or a StrEnum) and use it for SiteSpec.status, SiteCandidate.status and by_status; keep ProfileStatus separate and document why the two vocabularies differ.

..summary: --format is an unconstrained string forced into a Literal via an unexplained type: ignore and never consumed

evidence: OutputConfig.format is Literal['json', 'markdown', 'both'] (config/models.py:92), but run_search/output_format and the Typer option are str | None (app.py:201,274).
app.py:314 does config.output.format = output_format  # type: ignore[assignment] with no explanation of why an arbitrary CLI string is safe.
A project-wide search finds config.output.format is never read, so the ignore hides a no-op option as well as a type error.

The sibling commands use different unvalidated vocabularies: history.py:24 promises table/json/csv and history.py:60 promises table/json, both annotated str, with unknown values silently falling through.
detail.suggestion: Introduce OutputFormat(StrEnum) (or click.Choice) used by OutputConfig.format, SearchRequest.output_format, run_search and the Typer option so Typer rejects unknown values; either wire the value into ResultProcessor.save_results or remove the option. Apply the same enum treatment to the two history --format options.

..summary: SiteHome.goto changes the semantics of BasePage.goto by making url optional and defaulting to the home page

evidence: BasePage.goto(self, url: str) navigates to an explicit URL (pom/base.py:14-16).
SiteHome.goto(self, url: str | None = None) -> None navigates to self.base_url when called with no argument (pages/site_base.py:21-22).
A BasePage-typed caller cannot rely on the same call shape or meaning, and the override is exported through pom/pages/__init__.py as part of the page-object contract.
detail.suggestion: Rename the subclass method to open_home(self) -> None and keep goto(url: str) as the inherited navigation contract, or give BasePage.goto the same optional-url semantics and document it; add a test that calls the method through a BasePage reference.
